findings.summary: Private fetch-delivery wrapper can be deleted without changing behavior.
findings.consequence: The method adds an extra asynchronous indirection around `#startFetchDelivery` but does not add retry, timeout, ownership, abort, serialization, or page-exit policy; future delivery changes have one more helper to inspect even though the real policy lives elsewhere.
findings.evidence: The owned method consists only of `async #deliverByFetch(body: string): Promise<boolean>` and `return await this.#startFetchDelivery(body).delivery`, so it unwraps the `delivery` promise returned by the real fetch helper without adding behavior.
findings.recommendation: Inline the call sites as `await this.#startFetchDelivery(body).delivery`, or keep a helper only if it owns a distinct policy that is not already implemented by `#startFetchDelivery`.
